turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What are some picnic foods that don't need a fridge?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hard cheeses, crackers, whole fruit, nuts and pasta salad with oil instead of mayo all hold up well.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Is chicken okay if it's out for a few hours?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not really. Cooked chicken shouldn't sit out more than two hours, or one hour if it's hot outside.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay so maybe skip the chicken / or bring it in a cooler.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A cooler with a couple of ice packs would keep it safe. Put it in the shade.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about something sweet?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Brownies or lemon bars travel really well. Avoid anything with whipped cream, it melts fast.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How do I keep bugs away from a picnic?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Keep food covered when nobody's eating, and set up away from trash cans and standing water.

turns.speaker: user

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: They help a little, mostly close by. A gentle breeze helps more, so a slightly windy spot is better.

option_sets.lead_in: I'm planning a picnic for my book club and I need help choosing a place.
options: The first one is the botanical garden, really pretty, but you have to pay to get in.
Then there's the lake park, free and big, but it gets noisy on weekends.
And the last option is my friend's backyard, which has a big table and real bathrooms.
moshi_comment: For a book club, being able to hear each other matters, so the noisy lake park might be a problem. The botanical garden is beautiful and calm, just check whether people mind the fee. Your friend's backyard is the most comfortable, especially with a table and bathrooms.
I'd lean toward the backyard, it's quiet and practical for a long chat. Is it a special occasion, though? If you want it to feel a bit more special, the botanical garden is worth the ticket.

option_sets.lead_in: We're doing a picnic for my son's class and I can't pick a main food.
options: One idea is little sandwiches, cut into shapes, with cheese and ham or peanut butter.
Another is homemade pizza slices, which kids love but might get cold and greasy.
Or we could do wraps with chicken and veggies that the kids roll up themselves.
The last idea is a big pasta salad that's easy to make ahead the night before.
moshi_comment: Shaped sandwiches are a classic for kids and easy to eat with your hands. Pizza is popular but gets messy once it's cold. The build your own wraps are fun, but with a whole class it could get chaotic.
I'd go with the little sandwiches, but are there any allergies in the class? If peanuts are an issue, skip the peanut butter and maybe add the pasta salad as a backup.
